articles.summary: Finance Business Budgeting in Nigeria: How to Build and Manage a Company Budget Oluwakemi Adesina September 29, 2026 Business budgeting in Nigeria helps you keep track of your income, expenses, and financial priorities. A good business budget gives you a clearer picture of how much your company can spend, save, or invest. It also helps you make better financial decisions and prepare for unexpected costs. In this guide, we’ll look at how to create and manage a practical budget for your business. What Is Business Budgeting? A business budget is a plan for how a company expects to earn and spend its money over a specific period. It helps you see what is coming in, what needs to go out, and whether the business can afford its plans. Budgeting is different from bookkeeping. Bookkeeping records what has already happened, while budgeting uses that information to plan what happens next. A budget is also different from a financial forecast. A budget is the original plan for what the business expects to earn and spend during a specific period. A forecast is a working estimate that can change as new information comes in. For example, if fuel costs increase or a client delays payment, you can update the forecast to reflect the change while keeping the original budget as a benchmark. Why Business Budgeting in Nigeria Matters Running a business without a budget can make it difficult to know what you can afford. A practical budget helps you plan ahead, control spending, and spot financial problems before they become bigger issues. It can help you: Plan for periods when sales may slow down. Control operating expenses before they reduce your margins. Prepare for payroll and other major payments ahead of time. Allocate money across inventory, marketing, logistics, and other priorities. Spot financial gaps early enough to adjust your plans. Compare actual results with what you originally planned. What Should a Company Budget Include? An effective company budget planning framework should give you a clear view of expected income, regular expenses, payroll, and costs that may not occur every month. An effective company budget planning framework should give you a clear picture of expected income and the different costs of running the business. It should cover regular expenses as well as costs that may only come up occasionally. 1. Revenue Start with how much money you expect the business to bring in. Where possible, break this down by source: Product and service sales: Income from your main business activities. Recurring revenue: Retainers, subscriptions, service fees, or ongoing client contracts. Contract income: Expected payments from confirmed contracts. Seasonal revenue: Periods when sales typically increase or slow down. 2. Fixed Costs These are expenses that generally stay the same regardless of how much you sell during a given period. They may include: Rent: Office space, warehouses, or shop fronts. Salaries: Base pay for existing employees. Software subscriptions: Accounting, CRM, payroll, and other business tools. Insurance: Relevant business or employee insurance costs. Professional fees: Accounting, legal, consulting, or audit fees. 3. Variable Costs These expenses usually change as business activity changes. They can include: Inventory: Stock or raw materials needed for production. Logistics: Dispatch fees, delivery costs, and transportation. Sales commissions: Payments linked to sales performance. Marketing: Advertising and campaign-related spending. Transaction costs: Fees that increase with sales or payment volume. 4. One-Time and Unexpected Costs Not every expense happens every month. Your budget should also make room for planned one-off purchases and unexpected costs. This could include buying a new generator, replacing office laptops, upgrading equipment, or dealing with a sudden machinery breakdown. How to Create a Business Budget Step by Step Good business financial planning starts with what you already know about the business. Look at your past numbers, make realistic assumptions about the future, and build the budget from there. Step 1: Review Historical Financial Data Start with the numbers you already have. Review bank statements, sales records, payroll records, and expense records from the last 6 to 12 months, if available. This gives you a realistic starting point instead of relying on guesswork. Step 2: Estimate Future Revenue Be realistic about how much money the business is likely to make. Separate confirmed income from potential deals and make your assumptions clear. Also consider when customers are likely to pay, not just when a sale is made. Step 3: List Fixed and Variable Expenses Separate your fixed expenses from costs that change with business activity. Knowing your minimum fixed overhead helps you understand how much the business needs each month just to keep operating. Step 4: Include Payroll Payroll is often one of the largest and least flexible recurring expenses. Include current salaries, planned hires, expected bonuses, and applicable employer contributions such as pension and other statutory obligations. Step 5: Add a Contingency Allowance Unexpected costs are part of running a business, so leave room for them in the budget. Think about the risks your business is most likely to face, such as equipment repairs, alternative power costs, urgent logistics, or delayed customer payments, and set aside an amount that reflects those risks. Step 6: Review the Budget Monthly A budget is only useful if you check it against what actually happened. Set aside time each month to compare your planned figures with your actual income and expenses. If something is higher or lower than expected, find out why and adjust early. How to Build a Monthly Business Budget A monthly budget helps you see what the business planned to spend and what actually happened. You can use a simple table like the one below and adjust the categories to fit your business. Budget Area Planned (₦) Actual (₦) Variance (₦) Total Revenue Payroll & Benefits Core Operations Marketing & Growth Technology & Software Other/Unexpected Expenses Net Financial Position Note: For long-term financial stability, always align your underlying accounting reporting frameworks

articles.summary: SingSaver, Singapore's Leading Personal Finance Platform, Launches Home Loans Segment janray.javellana 29-Sep-2026 SingSaver, Singapore's Leading Personal Finance Platform, Launches Home Loans Segment 29-Sep-2026 General Affiliate partnership with Redbrick Mortgage Advisory gives SingSaver users bank-by-bank rate comparison and advice through to application The launch takes SingSaver into Singapore's largest household debt category, worth S$296.4 billion, where the gap between bank home loan rates and the HDB concessionary rate of 2.6% can add up to hundreds of dollars a month for borrowers SINGAPORE, Sept. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SingSaver , Singapore's leading personal finance comparison platform and part of Nasdaq-listed MoneyHero Group (NASDAQ: MNY), today launched a Home Loans comparison category in partnership with Redbrick Mortgage Advisory . The launch takes SingSaver into the largest category of household debt in Singapore and extends its product suite beyond credit cards, personal loans, insurance and brokerage. Under the partnership, SingSaver contributes its brand and high-intent user base, connecting Singaporeans researching home loans with Redbrick's comparison and advisory service. Redbrick manages the underlying bank panel and broker relationships, handling the process from comparison through to application. Home loans represent Singapore's single largest household debt category. Outstanding home loans reached S$296.4 billion in the first quarter of 2026. This accounted for approximately 71% of total household debt. The balance has grown for ten consecutive quarters, according to data released by the Department of Statistics (SingStat) and the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS). A Shifting Rate Environment The partnership lands at a point when the cost of not comparing has become easy to quantify. Three-month compounded Singapore Overnight Rate Average (SORA), the benchmark banks use to price most floating-rate mortgages, stood around 1.19% in mid-September 2026 . Bank mortgage packages have followed suit, with rates across major lenders now well below the HDB concessionary rate of 2.6% , which has not changed since Q2 of 2026. For a borrower with S$800,000 outstanding, the difference between 2.6% and 1.4% is roughly S$454 a month, or about S$5,400 a year. On a S$300,000 HDB loan, it is closer to S$170 a month. That arithmetic is driving a refinancing wave, concentrated among HDB flat owners whose lock-in periods have expired and who are comparing bank packages for the first time. "Home loans are the single biggest financial commitment most Singaporeans will make, yet the market has stayed fragmented and hard to compare. Redbrick is one of the most established names in mortgage advisory in Singapore, and this partnership closes a genuine gap in our platform at a time when falling rates are pushing more homeowners to actively shop around," said Ayush Goyal, Managing Director at SingSaver. "Redbrick's role has always been to give Singaporean homeowners impartial, expert guidance through one of the biggest financial decisions they will make. This partnership puts that guidance in front of a much wider pool of homeowners, right at the point they start comparing their options, and lets more people access the high standard of advice we've built our name on,” said Eugene Huang, Co-founder and director of Redbrick Mortgage Advisory . The launch builds on growth SingSaver has already seen in higher-ticket lending, including its personal loans and brokerage categories, and positions the platform in one of the largest consumer lending markets in Singapore. The Home Loans category is now live on SingSaver’s website here . The Company operates in Singapore, Hong Kong, Taiwan and the Philippines. Its brand portfolio includes B2C platforms MoneyHero, SingSaver, Money101, Moneymax and Seedly, as well as the B2B platform Creatory. MoneyHero had over 280 commercial partner relationships as at June 30, 2026, and had approximately 3.7 million Monthly Unique Users across its platform for the three months ended June 30, 2026. The Company’s backers include Peter Thiel—co-founder of PayPal, Palantir Technologies, and the Founders Fund—and Hong Kong businessman, Richard Li, the founder and chairman of Pacific Century Group. articles.summary: Alcon Highlights Its Comprehensive Innovation Portfolio at AAO 2026 sandra.hoffer Tue, 09/29/2026 - 14:52 Monday, October 5, 2026 Hands-on booth demonstrations of the UNITY platform showcase next-generation surgical advancements Recent innovations also include Clareon PanOptix Pro intraocular lenses and Valeda PBM for AMD, reflecting the breadth of innovation across Alcon's portfolio FORT WORTH, October 5, 2026 — Alcon (SIX/NYSE: ALC), the global leader in eye care dedicated to helping people see brilliantly, will highlight its innovation portfolio at the 2026 American Academy of Ophthalmology (AAO) annual meeting, October 10-12 in New Orleans. Attendees visiting Alcon at Booth #1519 can explore hands-on demonstrations spanning cataract, retina, glaucoma and dry eye disease. Featured innovations include the UNITY® platform, highlighted by the new UNITY® M ophthalmic microscope, along with Clareon® PanOptix® Pro, Clareon® TruPlus® IOLs, Valeda™ Photobiomodulation (PBM) and Voyager™ DSLT. "At AAO 2026, Alcon will demonstrate how innovation is redefining what's possible in eye care," said Sergio Duplan, President of the Americas at Alcon. "Attendees will experience firsthand how our portfolio is helping shape the future of eye care through technologies and clinical solutions that support eye care professionals every day." UNITY Booth Demonstrations Provide a Firsthand Look at Alcon's Surgical Platform The UNITY platform will anchor Alcon's AAO presence. Attendees can participate in private demonstrations of both configurations: the UNITY VCS combined console and the UNITY CS standalone cataract system. The recently launched UNITY® M microscope, a premium surgical microscope that delivers precise control for ophthalmic surgeons, will also be featured. Together, these experiences provide a firsthand look at how connected surgical technologies support visualization, workflow efficiency and surgical performance. Alcon experts will be available for one-on-one discussions and product demonstrations throughout the meeting. Recent Innovations Demonstrate Alcon's Broad Eye Care Portfolio Alcon's booth will also feature demonstrations highlighting several of the company's newest innovations. In cataract surgery, attendees can learn more about Clareon PanOptix Pro, the latest evolution of the world's leading trifocal family, as well as Clareon TruPlus IOLs, Alcon's next-generation monofocal and toric IOL platform designed to build on the performance of the Clareon family. In retina, attendees can explore Valeda PBM, the first and only FDA-authorized treatment for patients with early and intermediate dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD), through dedicated technology demonstrations.1 In glaucoma, Alcon will showcase Voyager DSLT, an innovative first-line glaucoma treatment option powered by automated SureTrac eye-tracking technology, which precisely delivers laser pulses through the limbus to the trabecular meshwork.2 In addition to its surgical portfolio, Alcon will highlight TRYPTYR® (acoltremon ophthalmic solution) 0.003%, a prescription treatment option for the millions of patients affected by dry eye disease (DED). As the first neuromodulator eye drop that can rapidly increase natural tear production as early as day one, TRYPTYR represents a novel approach to DED management.3-7 Attendees can learn more about this innovation, including its first-in-class mechanism of action, by visiting Alcon at booth #1519. For more information about Alcon's presence at AAO 2026, including demonstrations, presentations and featured innovations, visit www.MyAlconatAAO.com . About Alcon Alcon helps people see brilliantly. As the global leader in eye care with a heritage spanning over 75 years, we offer the broadest portfolio of products to enhance sight and improve people’s lives. Our Surgical and Vision Care products touch the lives of more than 260 million people in over 140 countries and territories each year living with conditions like cataracts, glaucoma, retinal diseases and refractive errors. Our more than 25,000 associates are enhancing the quality of life through innovative products, partnerships with Eye Care Professionals and programs that advance access to quality eye care. Learn more at www.alcon.com . Connect with us on Facebook and LinkedIn . About TRYPTYR® (acoltremon ophthalmic solution) 0.003% INDICATIONS AND USAGE TRYPTYR® (acoltremon ophthalmic solution) 0.003% is indicated for the treatment of the signs and symptoms of dry eye disease (DED). IMPORTANT SAFETY INFORMATION Warnings and Precautions Potential for Eye Injury and Contamination: To avoid the potential for eye injury and contamination, advise patients not to touch the vial tip to the eye or other surfaces. Use with Contact Lenses: TRYPTYR should not be administered while wearing contact lenses. If contact lenses are worn, they should be removed prior to administration of the solution. Lenses may be reinserted 15 minutes following administration of TRYPTYR. Adverse Reactions In clinical trials, the most common adverse reaction was instillation site pain (50%). Please click here for the TRYPTYR Full Prescribing Information. About Valeda® PBM The Valeda Light Delivery System improves visual acuity in patients with best-corrected visual acuity of 20/32 through 20/70 and who have dry age-related macular degeneration (AMD) characterized by: 1. The presence of at least 3 medium drusen (> 63 μm and ≤ 125 μm in diameter), or large drusen (> 125 μm in diameter), or non-central geographic atrophy, and 2. The absence of neovascular maculopathy or central-involving geographic atrophy. Do not treat patients with Valeda if they have any known photosensitivity to yellow light, red light, or near-infrared radiation (NIR), have a history of light-activated central nervous system disorders (e.g., epilepsy, migraine), or within 30 days of using photosensitizing agents. Treatment benefit may not persist significantly after treatment is stopped. No significant data on the safety and effectiveness for more frequent or extended treatments beyond described in operator’s manual. About UNITY® VCS and CS The UNITY® VCS (Vitreoretinal Cataract System) console, when used with compatible devices, is indicated for use during anterior segment (i.e., phacoemulsification and removal of cataracts) and posterior segment (i.e., vitreoretinal) ophthalmic surgery. The UNITY® CS (Cataract System) console, when used with compatible devices, is indicated for use during anterior segment (i.e., phacoemulsification and removal of cataracts) ophthalmic surgery. Refer to the Directions for Use for the accessories/consumables and User Manual for a complete listing of indications, warnings, cautions and notes. About UNITY® M UNITY® M is the latest ophthalmic microscope available by Alcon. As with all ophthalmic microscopes, exposure during aphakia should be limited to reduce the risk of damage. During aphakia and at maximum illumination intensity, limit exposure to red reflex light to no more than 9.6 minutes. About Clareon® PanOptix® Pro The Clareon PanOptix Pro Trifocal IOL is a type of multifocal IOL used to focus images clearly onto the back of your eye (retina) to allow clear vision after the cataract removal. In addition, the center of the Clareon PanOptix Pro Trifocal IOL allows for better near (reading) vision and intermediate (computer work) vision versus what a monofocal lens would provide. Potential Side Effects: Due to the design of multifocal IOLs, there are some side effects that can be associated with the Clareon PanOptix Pro Trifocal IOL models. These may be worse than with a monofocal IOL, including visual disturbances such as glare, rings around lights, starbursts (rays around light sources), and reduced contrast sensitivity (decreased ability to distinguish objects from their background, especially in dim lighting). These side effects may make it more difficult to see while driving at night or completing tasks in low lighting conditions such as at night or in fog or in a dimly lit room after surgery, as compared to before surgery. articles.summary: Alcon and Aravind: Expanding Access Through Education bethany.dickinson Tue, 09/29/2026 - 21:08 Story Headline Alcon and Aravind: Expanding Access Through Education Story Teaser Summary Expanding access to quality eye care starts with expanding access to quality education. Through a longstanding partnership with Aravind Eye Care System, Alcon is helping equip Eye Care Professionals with the skills and training needed to serve more patients around the world. Story Date Thu, 10/01/2026 - 12:00 Featured 1 Category Vision for the World Hero image Expanded access to quality eye care for patients starts with expanded access to quality surgical training and education for doctors. For more than 20 years, Alcon and Aravind Eye Care System have worked together to advance ophthalmic education and support the development of Eye Care Professionals. Together, Alcon and Aravind share a belief that strengthening clinical skills and expanding access to training can help build the capacity needed to meet growing patient needs today and in the future. That commitment reached a new milestone in July 2026 with the launch of the Aravind Retina Centre of Excellence in Coimbatore, India, a dedicated training facility designed to expand retina education, facilitate knowledge exchange and provide hands-on learning opportunities for Eye Care Professionals in India and beyond. As retinal diseases affect an estimated 11 million people in India,1 the need for specialized retinal care continues to grow. Addressing that need requires more than technology alone — it requires investing in the people who deliver care. Through advanced training programs, peer-to-peer learning and access to modern surgical techniques, the Retina Centre of Excellence is designed to help physicians strengthen their skills and bring high-quality retinal care to more patients and communities. This focus on education builds on the success of a longstanding collaboration. In 2024, Alcon and Aravind launched the Global Centre of Excellence for advanced cataract surgery training, helping equip surgeons with the skills and technologies needed to deliver high-quality care. Since its launch, more than 580 doctors from 42 countries have participated in training opportunities designed to advance clinical expertise and improve patient outcomes. The need for continued investment in workforce development remains significant. While demand for retinal services continues to increase, only an estimated 5% with many concentrated in major metropolitan areas.2 By expanding opportunities for education and hands-on learning, Alcon and Aravind are helping strengthen the clinical workforce needed to support more patients in more places. "Training has always been one of the most powerful ways to create lasting impact in eye care. By combining Aravind's expertise in education with Alcon's innovation, we have an opportunity to strengthen clinical capabilities, expand access to specialized care and ultimately help more people preserve and restore their sight." Dr. S. Aravind, Chief Medical Officer, Aravind Eye Care System “As we approach World Sight Day, we celebrate the power of partnership, education and shared expertise to create a lasting impact. articles.summary: Model routers are everywhere right now, but they have a fundamental limitation. No matter if based on advanced heuristics or a small model that reads each turn and picks which LLM to use, a router will always be less capable than the model it’s choosing for. Replit Agent lets the model decide instead. The main agent, or core loop, chooses its subagents’ tier and effort, and adjusts its own as the task unfolds. Given that freedom, GPT-6 Astra hands routine implementation to less costly subagents and decides for itself where its tokens are worth spending. On both DeepSWE and Terminal-Bench, Replit Agent is Pareto-efficient against Astra on its own: no published Astra baseline costs less and scores higher. It also beats a sidekick architecture, the same setup with one long-lived worker, by 11 and 16 points. Why we scaffold less Every model release invalidates assumptions baked into the harness. As models become stronger at long-horizon tasks, they don’t need as much scaffolding at the harness layer. In practice, we’ve observed them lean more towards delegation on their own: using subagents for context management and parallelism. Recent breakthroughs, Navier–Stokes among them, came in part from coordinating swarms of agents powered by frontier models [1]. But the frontier is jagged. The strongest coding model is not necessarily the strongest at designing UIs or making slides, nor the best at writing emails. So we design our harness to let each model work its own way, with the guardrails it still needs and quality at minimum cost as the goal.
articles.title: Free the models: Harness design at the frontier
